attempts.label: DANDI:002034
attempts.paper_title: Limitations of pupil diameter as a proxy for modes of locus coeruleus activity
attempts.entry_title: LC firing and pupil diameter, baseline and evoked (Thompson & Gold 2026)
attempts.summary: The paper's main findings held up in this data. Baseline LC firing and baseline pupil covary, as do evoked LC and evoked pupil responses, and each evoked response falls with its own baseline. Neither baseline reliably predicts the other signal's evoked response, per unit (Figure 2) and pooled (Figure 3), assuming as the paper's code does that the files' trial start marks fixation onset. Of the minor analyses, the raw-baseline control held in part, while a link between baseline LC and the range of evoked pupil in one monkey and a linear against quadratic fit comparison did not reproduce. Both appear only with the code's evoked pupil window and trial rule, which differ from the Methods.
attempts.description: Tests the findings of Thompson and Gold (2026) on dandiset 002034, which holds the 83 sessions of LC single units and pupil diameter from two monkeys in a passive fixation task with occasional beeps. It recomputes the within-epoch and cross-epoch correlations of Figure 2, the range analysis, the raw-baseline version of Supplemental Figure 1, the linear against quadratic fits of Supplemental Figure 2 and the pooled analysis of Figure 3, under the Methods' measures and under the paper's code.

outcomes.statement: The dandiset's sessions and units are those of the paper's code (its include lists), and the code's pipeline, run on the dandiset, gives the statistics the code printed for it.

outcomes.quote: All data and analysis code necessary to generate figures is accessible at https://github.com/lwthompson2/Thompson2026_LCPupilAnalysis.git.
outcomes.notes: All 83 sessions and 105 units on the code's include lists are in the dandiset and every dandiset unit is listed. The code's pipeline rewritten in Python and run on the dandiset matches 26 of 26 values the code printed (3974 beep and 15770 fixation trial rows, the twelve Figure 2 tests, the four range correlations, the eight LLR counts); the only visible difference is Ci row 1, p = 1.14e-5 against the printed 1.18e-5. The code's twelve printed Figure 3 pooled coefficients are matched to its three decimals (12 of 12) when firing rates are z-scored by within-session unit index across sessions, as zscore_tables.m does; z-scored per unit, 2 of 12 match.

outcomes.notes: With raw baselines 11 of 12 row and monkey cells match the Figure 2 pattern under E1 and under E2 (T1); the cell that differs is row 6 in Ci (median -0.006, p = 0.14). The code reading matches all 12. Under T2, E2 matches 10. Leaving out beep trials whose 200 ms evoked window runs past the end of the trial (variant) also gives 11 of 12, with the same cell differing (p = 0.13). Row 6 does not use the evoked pupil, and it fails under both mixtures (code trials with E1, p = 0.131; Methods trials with the code's evoked pupil, p = 0.136), so the code's 12 of 12 comes from its trial set, not its pupil window. The code reading without beep trials whose 200 ms window runs past the end gives row 6 Ci with raw baselines median -0.018, p = 0.12, not significant, so the code's match on this cell (p = 0.023) rests on evoked rates that are likely biased low. Code-rule trials whose beep falls after the end of the trial enter no table, since they have no evoked pupil.

outcomes.quote: we applied our single-unit analyses (Figure 2) to data pooled across all trials, sessions, and units (Figure 3). The results are qualitatively similar for the pooled and single-unit analyses
outcomes.notes: All four within-epoch columns give p < 0.05 in the sign of the Figure 2 row in both monkeys under E1 and E2 (8 of 8 cells), for example column 1 Oz rho = 0.090, Ci 0.063; column 3 Oz -0.38, Ci -0.39 under E1; also under every variant and the code's z-scoring. With raw baselines (variant) column 1 is not significant in Ci (rho = 0.005, p = 0.6). Pupil z-scored again per session (variant) and the variant without beep trials whose 200 ms evoked window runs past the end of the trial also give 8 of 8.
deviations: Beep trials follow the Methods' rule (at least 100 ms of baseline, Methods, Pupillometry and Neuronal Recordings) and need one evoked pupil window before 20 ms from the end of fixation (implied by the Methods' window, stated here); fixation-only baseline rates end 20 ms before the end of the trial (Methods, Neuronal Recordings). The code's rule (beep more than 400 ms after the start and 800 ms before the end of the padded pupil record) and windows are a variant.

The evoked pupil is read as the Methods describe it (50 ms windows in 10 ms steps from the beep to 20 ms before the end of fixation), as E1 and E2 (claims file); the code measures it over 0 to 800 ms after the beep with a centred 50 ms moving mean, shown as a variant.
Firing rates are z-scored per unit (the Figure 3 legend and the claims file); the code groups by within-session unit index, shown as a variant.

Assumption. Pupil is used as stored, taken as already z-scored per session (Methods, Pupillometry); the data check is consistent with this but the files do not say so, and the pooled coefficients mix sessions, so they rest on it. Pupil z-scored again per session (variant) changes them by at most 0.008. Asked of the paper's authors (findings).

The trial start is taken as fixation onset for every window, as the paper's code does; the files hold no fixation marker and do not say what event the trial start marks, the beep falls a median 2.2 s after it against the Methods' 1 to 1.5 s of fixation, and 39% of spikes are stored before it, so the start may precede fixation onset (data check). Asked of the paper's authors (findings).

outcomes.quote: in neither case showing a reliable relationship between baseline pupil and evoked LC responses or baseline LC activity and evoked pupil responses across monkeys. This result also held when LC units were separated based on the direction of their baseline relationship with pupil size

Ci's negative group (4 units) shows evoked LC falling with baseline pupil (rho = -0.17, p = 0.012), not seen in Oz's 3 units (p = 0.91). Neither unit the code removes as rows 43 and 65 is in a row 1 group under any reading (row 1 p = 0.15 to 0.42), so groups formed after the code's removal are the same and give the same result (0 cells significant with one sign in both monkeys), as does pupil z-scored again per session.

Pupil is used as stored, taken as already z-scored per session (Methods, Pupillometry); the data check is consistent with this but the files do not say so, and the pooled coefficients mix sessions, so they rest on it. Pupil z-scored again per session (variant) gives the same result. Asked of the paper's authors (findings).

Groups are the units whose row 1 partial correlation has p < 0.05 (12 positive and 3 negative in Oz, 17 and 4 in Ci under the Methods' trials), taken from all units in place of the code's table after its removal of two units; neither removed unit is in a group under any reading (printed).

Assumption. The trial start is taken as fixation onset for every window, as the paper's code does; the files hold no fixation marker and do not say what event the trial start marks, the beep falls a median 2.2 s after it against the Methods' 1 to 1.5 s of fixation, and 39% of spikes are stored before it, so the start may precede fixation onset (data check). Asked of the paper's authors (findings).

findings.statement: The code's include list already lacks units 43 and 65 of the legacy numbering (its unit_id runs 1 to 107 without them), and prepare_figure_analysis_tables.m (build_stats) then removes rows 43 and 65 of its own 105-row table again, which drops CiCM101019d unit 1 and Ci_LC_d14_6mm_SC_123107 unit 2. This is why the code's printed output has 61 Ci units and 50 Ci sessions for some analyses against the paper's 63 and 51.

zscore_tables.m z-scores firing rates per value of the within-session unit index (unit 1, 2 or 3) pooled across all sessions and both monkeys, not per unit as the Figure 3 legend says (z-scored separately for each session/unit). Run here this way, the code's pipeline gives all 12 of the code's printed Figure 3 pooled coefficients to their three decimals; z-scored per unit, 2 of 12. Per unit the conclusions are the same.

The code measures the evoked pupil over 0 to 800 ms after the beep with a centred 50 sample moving mean, where the Methods give 50 ms windows in 10 ms steps from the beep to 20 ms before the end of fixation; it keeps beep trials more than 400 ms after the trial start and 800 ms before the end of the NaN-padded pupil record, where the Methods ask for 100 ms of baseline, so it keeps trials whose beep falls near or after the end of the trial (those after the end have no evoked pupil and enter no table, but 85 beep rows with the beep 7 to 69 ms before the end do); and it counts fixation-only baseline spikes to the end of the trial, not 20 ms before it. Under the Methods' measures two claims do not reproduce (the Oz range effect of rho = -0.33 and the cross-epoch LLR counts) and a third only in part, while the code reproduces the paper's numbers. On those 85 rows most of the 200 ms evoked rate window lies past the end of the trial, where spikes are mostly not stored, so their evoked rates are likely biased low; without beep trials whose 200 ms window runs past the end, the code reading no longer reproduces row 6 in Ci with raw baselines (p = 0.12, Supplemental Figure 1). Question for the authors: which window and trial rule produced the reported numbers?

The pupil series (acquisition pupil_value_channel4, unit a.u.) is not described beyond its source variable. Its values are consistent with the Methods' preprocessing having been applied before deposit (per session mean near 0 and SD 0.80 to 0.99, the mean trace across trials within 0.19 of 0, smooth at 1 ms), but the file does not say so. The trial table's trial_time_index has no unit (milliseconds by its range, 4 to 61 min per session), the files do not say what event the trial start marks, spike times are given against artificial trial anchors 100 s apart (spike_time_policy), and every trial is marked correct, so the files appear to hold correct trials only without saying so.

Beep times run from about 1.0 to 2.8 s after the trial start (5th to 95th percentile; 8.8% of Oz and 4.4% of Ci beeps fall within 1 to 1.5 s), against the Methods' beep after 1 to 1.5 s of fixation; 8 beeps fall before the trial start and 83 after its end. 26% of Oz and 7% of Ci fixation-only trials last under 1 s (shortest 206 ms), against the Methods' fixation of 1 to 5 s. About 39% of spikes are stored in the few seconds before a trial's start (median 0.8 s before it) and under 2% after its end, with the rate falling from 4.4 sp/s in the last 200 ms of a trial to 0.85 sp/s in the 200 ms after it, so on the beep trials with less than 200 ms between the beep and the end (75 of 914 Oz and 96 of 2161 Ci beep trials under the Methods' rule, more under the code's) the 0 to 200 ms evoked rate is counted partly over a period without stored spikes.

The session Cicero_022714_d18_402_FixnStim is named for stimulation, but no file has a stimulation marker column, so whether any of its trials carried microstimulation cannot be told; the code's rule for fixation-only trials (no beep and no stimulation marker) then keeps all of its non-beep trials.

The Results name a Wilcoxon rank-sum test for the one-sample hypothesis that the median coefficient is 0; the code runs the signed-rank test (signrank), whose p-values equal the printed ones. The Results also relate the coefficients to the range in each session, while the code takes the range per unit.

Three choices that the outcomes here rest on are assumptions, asked of the paper's authors. First, which event does the trial start in the files mark? Every window is taken from it as fixation onset, as the code does, but the files hold no fixation marker, the beep falls a median 2.2 s after the start against the Methods' 1 to 1.5 s of fixation, and 39% of spikes are stored before it. Second, is the stored pupil trace already z-scored per session, with the mean trace subtracted and smoothed, as the Methods describe? The values are consistent with it, and the pooled Figure 3 coefficients rest on it. Third, which units and sessions did the paper use: its 63 units in 51 Ci sessions, or the 61 in 50 of the code's output? Row 6 in Ci is fragile on this point.

entries.name: 002034-thompson-2026
entries.title: LC firing and pupil diameter, baseline and evoked (Thompson & Gold 2026)
entries.description: Tests the findings of Thompson and Gold (2026) on dandiset 002034, which holds the 83 sessions of LC single units and pupil diameter from two monkeys in a passive fixation task with occasional beeps. It recomputes the within-epoch and cross-epoch correlations of Figure 2, the range analysis, the raw-baseline version of Supplemental Figure 1, the linear against quadratic fits of Supplemental Figure 2 and the pooled analysis of Figure 3, under the Methods' measures and under the paper's code.
